reading.body:
Profit Finder Pro Software is not a data center and should not be counted in any assessment of AI infrastructure or grid load.

The listing is a customer relationship management and sales-tracking product sold to small businesses in roofing, solar, contracting, and insurance. Its address in the Scottsdale area of Maricopa County, Arizona is currently occupied by a different company, TraVek Inc. Nothing publicly available connects the software business or that address to server infrastructure, colocation space, or dedicated data center equipment. The entry originates as a mistagged OpenStreetMap point labeled telecom=data_center, and no specifications are published for it.

The pattern matters because capacity maps are only as good as their weakest row. A single mistagged small-business address can enter a dataset, inherit a facility shape, and sit alongside real sites without any of the physical markers that make a data center a data center: published power draw, operator, or equipment. Here the published capacity is zero megawatts, and the research status is exhausted, meaning the absence of a connection to server infrastructure is a finding rather than a gap.

What this does not tell the reader is anything about Arizona's actual data center footprint. The state's four facilities with published figures total 512 MW, and this entry contributes none of it. It also does not establish that the address lacks power or fiber, only that no public source ties it to data center operations. The coordinates sit 14.5 miles from Phoenix Sky Harbor International Airport and several miles from the other rows in the same batch, so no shared building links them.
